Error.description: Campus error envelope (see ErrorEnvelope); malformed or invalid fields use the ValidationError shape (422, with error.errors). Possible statuses: 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 415, 422, 429, 500, 503.

code.description: Campus error code (UPPER_SNAKE_CASE; AUTH_* for OAuth protocol errors, RFC 6749 §5.2)

details.description: Additional error details, including OAuth protocol fields (error, error_description)

errors.description: Field-level validation errors; present on the 422 ValidationError shape only

code.description: Machine-readable field error code, e.g. MISSING, INVALID_TYPE, UNRECOGNIZED_FIELD

info.description:
Campus OAuth 2.0 authorization server and authentication API.

The API has two provider families with deliberately different
mechanics (docs/auth-token-invariants.md):

- `campus` (first-party): Campus's own OAuth 2.0 authorization
  server — authorization-code, device-code (RFC 8628) and refresh
  grants issuing Campus bearer tokens.
- `google`, `github`, `discord` (third-party): OAuth proxies that
  carry out browser login/consent with the upstream provider and
  keep custody of the upstream credentials. Upstream access tokens
  are released to apps only through the token bridge
  (docs/token-broker.md); refresh tokens never leave Campus.

## Trails

- docs/auth-login-flow.md — the browser login chain
- docs/token-broker.md — the token bridge contract
- docs/auth-token-invariants.md — security invariants
- campus/auth/docs/auth-error-spec.md — error codes

## Error responses

Errors use the Campus error envelope (see `ErrorEnvelope`), with
`AUTH_*` error codes; RFC 6749 protocol errors surface in
`error.details` with the OAuth error string. Malformed request
bodies return the validation-error shape (`ValidationError`).
There are no endpoint-specific exceptions (#714 normalized the
last flat-shape holdouts on `/root/` and the vault lookup).

## Trailing slashes

Paths are listed exactly as routed (Flask): a path shown with a
trailing slash must be requested with it — the no-slash variant
answers with a 308 redirect.
info.title: Campus Auth API

get.description:
Browser endpoint. Validates the request (fail-closed
redirect_uri matching, RFC 6749 section 3.1.2.2), then
redirects to the Google leg for authentication. `scope` must
be within the session's scopes — violations are rejected with
400 `invalid_scope` without redirecting. Login never carries
upstream scopes (#733): the retired `upstream_scope` parameter
has been removed; requests carrying it fail validation with
422. On success: 302 to `/auth/v1/google/authorize?...`.

https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-4.1.1

Summary: 
    OAuth2 authorization endpoint for user consent and code grant.
    1. Validates the authorization request
    2. Authenticates the user (through Google Workspace)
    3. Verifies scope of consent
    4. Issues authorization code
    5. Redirects user to the specified redirect URI

Method:
    GET /authorize

Path Parameters:
    None

Query parameters:
    - client_id: ID of OAuth client requesting authorization
    - response_type: str (required)
        Must be "code" for authorization code flow.
    - redirect_uri: str (required)
        URI to redirect the user to after authentication
    - scope: str (optional)
        Space-separated list of Campus scopes requested by the
        client; must be within the session's scopes.
    - state: str
        Opaque value used by the client to maintain state between
        request and callback.
        Typically used to pass a session ID or target; Campus uses
        it as session ID

Responses:
    400 invalid_scope: None
    - Returned when the request's scope parameter exceeds the
      scopes granted in the referenced auth session.
    404 Session not found: None
    - Returned when the user session is not found and user needs to
      log in.
    401 Invalid client_id/user_id: None
    - Returned when the client_id or user_id in the session does not
      match the request.
    400 Invalid request: None
    - Returned (without redirecting) when the client has no
      registered redirect_uris, when the request's redirect_uri does
      not exactly match a registered URI (RFC 6749 §3.1.2.2), or
      when the session's redirect_uri does not match the request.
    302 Found: Redirect
    - Redirects to the specified redirect URI with the
      authorization code, as well as state if provided.
      e.g. /oauth2/authorize?code=abc123&state=xyz

post.description:
The only sanctioned path to upstream (e.g. Google) access
tokens — docs/token-broker.md. Requires a campus Bearer token
for the user, presented by a confidential client flagged
`token_bridge` (invariant C1; anything else is 403). The
response carries the access token, its expiry and its scope —
never a refresh token (C2). `min_scopes` must be within the
client's `upstream_scopes[provider]` allowlist (400) and
covered by the user's stored grant (403 with `missing_scopes`
and a re-consent hint, C3).

POST /broker/{provider}
Auth: campus Bearer token (the user), issued to a confidential
client flagged for bridge access.
Body: {
    "min_scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/classroom.rosters"]
    # Optional: scopes the caller requires. Denied unless the user's
    # upstream grant covers them AND the client's upstream_scopes
    # allowlist permits them.
}
Returns: {
    "provider": "google",
    "user_id": "user@nyjc.edu.sg",
    "access_token": "<upstream access token>",
    "token_type": "Bearer",
    "expires_in": 1234,
    "scope": "email profile https://..."
}

The refresh token is never included: Campus refreshes silently via
its stored credential and remains the sole custodian. Tokens are
released for in-memory use until expiry only — downstream apps must
not persist them (invariant D1).
post.summary: Release the user's upstream access token

post.description:
Per-integration variant of the token bridge (#733): releases
the user's credential for the integration's namespaced provider
(e.g. `google.classroom`) via the integration's own OAuth
client, refreshing silently server-side. Same C1 guards as the
identity route. Amended C3a rule: the client's
`upstream_scopes` must carry a NON-EMPTY entry for the
namespaced provider even when `min_scopes` is omitted (absent
key ⇒ 400 — an integration token inherently carries
integration scopes). `min_scopes` are additionally capped by
the integration's vault `SCOPES` set (400). Unknown slug,
base-provider mismatch, or unconfigured integration ⇒ 404; no
stored credential ⇒ 404 with a hint pointing at the connect
flow; grant misses `min_scopes` ⇒ 403 with `missing_scopes`.

POST /broker/{provider}/{integration}
e.g. POST /broker/google/classroom/
Auth: campus Bearer token (the user), issued to a confidential
client flagged for bridge access (same guards as the identity
route, invariant C1).
Body: {"min_scopes": ["..."]}  (optional)
Returns: same shape as the identity route, with the namespaced
provider string (e.g. "google.classroom"); no refresh token, ever
(invariant B2).

Integration-specific rules (#733, design §2.4-§2.5):
- The caller's upstream_scopes must carry a NON-EMPTY entry for the
  namespaced provider even when min_scopes is omitted: an
  integration token inherently carries integration scopes, so an
  absent entry means no access at all (fail-closed).
- min_scopes are additionally capped by the integration's vault
  SCOPES set; asking beyond it is a configuration error.
- A missing user credential is a 404 whose hint points at the
  connect flow, not at the deprecated upstream_scope login path.
post.summary: Release the user's stored integration access token

post.description:
The response never contains a secret; the first secret is
obtained (and later rotated) via `POST /clients/{client_id}/revoke`.
Scope fields are fail-closed (docs/auth-token-invariants.md A1/B3/C1).

POST /clients/
Authorization: operator only, plus designated admin users holding
clients:admin (#865) — client registration mints a new principal.

Body: {
    "name": "Client Name",
    "description": "Client description",
    "is_public": false,  # Optional: true for CLI/mobile apps
    "redirect_uris": [],  # Optional: OAuth redirect URIs
    "allowed_scopes": [],  # Optional: scope allowlist (fail-closed)
    "upstream_scopes": {},  # Optional: per-provider upstream allowlist
    "token_bridge": false  # Optional: upstream token release access
}

Returns: {
    "id": "client_abc123",
    "name": "Client Name",
    "description": "Client description",
    "is_public": false,
    "redirect_uris": [],
    "allowed_scopes": [],
    "upstream_scopes": {},
    "token_bridge": false,
    "created_at": "2025-07-20T10:30:00Z"
}

Public clients (is_public=true) don't have a client_secret and are used
for CLI, mobile apps, and native applications that cannot securely store
credentials per RFC 6749 Section 2.1.

allowed_scopes is the fail-closed scope allowlist
(docs/auth-token-invariants.md A1): a client with an empty allowlist
can be granted no scopes. upstream_scopes caps the third-party
provider scopes a client may be granted through the OAuth proxies
(invariant B3); an absent provider entry allows only that proxy's
base scopes. token_bridge grants access to the upstream token
release endpoint (invariant C1): confidential clients only, never
public ones.

patch.description:
`is_public` cannot be changed after creation. Public clients cannot be granted `token_bridge`. Authorization
    (#881, #888): the operator principal, or a designated admin user holding a `clients` grant row
    (access-grant store, `/auth/v1/grants`) whose token carries the scope — `clients:write` for benign
    fields (name, description, redirect_uris). The scope caps and `token_bridge` are operator-only for
    users: grant rows cap at `clients:write` (#883 decision 4). Client principals are read-only on their own
    records — their PATCH is rejected with 403 pointing at the user-principal path.

PATCH /clients/{client_id}
Authorization: the operator may update everything (#854);
designated admin users may update benign fields with clients:write
and the scope caps with clients:admin (#865). Client principals
are read-only on client records, including their own (#881):
mutating registration data must be attributable to a user, so a
client-principal PATCH is rejected (403) with the error pointing
at the clients:write user-principal path.

Body: {
    "name": "New Client Name",
    "description": "New description",
    "redirect_uris": ["urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob"],  # Optional
    "allowed_scopes": ["read", "write"],  # Optional
    "upstream_scopes": {"google": [...]}  # Optional
}
Returns: {
    "id": "client_abc123",
    "name": "New Client Name",
    "description": "New description",
    "is_public": false,
    "redirect_uris": [],
    "allowed_scopes": [],
    "upstream_scopes": {},
    "created_at": "2025-07-20T10:30:00Z"
}

Note: is_public cannot be changed after client creation.
allowed_scopes is the fail-closed scope allowlist
(docs/auth-token-invariants.md A1): sessions and device codes may
only request scopes it contains. upstream_scopes caps the
third-party provider scopes the client may be granted through the
OAuth proxies (invariant B3). allowed_scopes, upstream_scopes and
token_bridge are operator-controlled: a designated admin user
needs clients:admin to set them, and client principals are
rejected on every PATCH (#881).

get.description:
Metadata-only inventory of the upstream credentials Campus
custodies for a user (#733 design §2.7) — the sanctioned
status surface for integrations pages. Campus bearer token:
self only. Basic auth: delegated access, requires `user_id`.
Campus login tokens are not connections (C5) and are not
listed; no token value is ever returned (C2).

GET /connections/
Auth: campus bearer token (self) or basic auth + user_id
(delegate). Under bearer auth the inventory is always the bearer's
own.
Returns: {
    "connections": [
        {
            "provider": "google.classroom",
            "integration": "classroom",  (null for identity providers)
            "scopes": ["..."],
            "connected_at": "<UTC datetime>",
            "expires_at": "<UTC datetime> | null"
        }
    ]
}

Campus login tokens are not connections (C5) and are not listed;
no token value is ever returned (C2).

delete.description:
Deletes every stored credential row for (provider, user)
together with its token records, and emits
`campus.integrations.disconnect` (no token values). Bearer
auth acts for its own user; basic auth requires `user_id`.
The next login or connect re-establishes the grant; 404 means
there was nothing to disconnect. `campus` is refused (403 —
campus tokens are revoked via /oauth/revoke, C5), and
namespaced providers (e.g. `google.classroom` in the provider
segment) are refused with a pointer to the integration route.

DELETE /connections/{provider}/   e.g. /connections/google/
Auth: campus bearer token (self) or basic auth + user_id
(delegate).
Returns: {} with 200

Browser endpoint: 302 to Google. `scope` (space-delimited)
requests upstream Google scopes beyond the base `email profile`
set; they are merged with `include_granted_scopes=true` so
re-consent accumulates (invariant B3). The app path reaches
this endpoint through `/authorize`, which caps `scope` against
the client's `upstream_scopes` allowlist first.

prompt defaults to select_account (#844): every identity login
must stop at Google's account chooser, so a browser that still
holds a Google session after logging out of a campus app cannot
silently re-authenticate as the previous user on the next app's
login. Standard SaaS SSO semantics: sign-out ends the campus
session, Google's stays alive, and the next login shows the
picker. Callers may still pass an explicit prompt query param
to override.

scope (space-delimited) requests upstream Google scopes beyond
the proxy's base set (email, profile), merged via
include_granted_scopes=true so re-consent accumulates
(invariant B3, docs/auth-token-invariants.md). The app path
reaches this endpoint through provider.authorize, which caps
the requested scopes against the campus client's
upstream_scopes allowlist before forwarding them here; what the
broker may later release is re-checked against the same
allowlist.

Browser endpoint (called by Google). Verifies the grant, enforces the workspace domain, stores the user's
    Google credential (access and refresh tokens, server-side only), sets the campus login cookie and 302s
    to the flow's `target`.

Dispatches to success or error handlers based on payload type.

Browser endpoint: 302 to Google under the integration's own
OAuth client (#733). Requires the browser to already hold a
campus session (401 otherwise) — connect binds the credential
to the session user, never an anonymous browser. `target` must
be an HTTPS origin in the integration's vault
`CONNECT_TARGETS`. Consent is forced (`prompt=consent`) so the
stored credential always carries a refresh token, and the
asked scopes are exactly the integration's vault `SCOPES` cap.

Guards (design §2.3), all enforced here, not just in the
calling app:
1. the browser must hold a campus session (the user logs in via
   the identity flow first);
2. the integration must be a registry entry with a configured
   vault client, and connect must be enabled (non-empty
   CONNECT_TARGETS);
3. the target must be an HTTPS origin in CONNECT_TARGETS.

Consent is forced (prompt=consent) so the stored credential
always carries a refresh token, the asked scopes are exactly
the vault SCOPES cap, and the redirect lands on the
integration's own callback path (each integration's Google
client registers its own callback URL in Google Cloud). Connect
is a user-session flow: no campus client allowlist applies
here; per-app policy is enforced at the broker.

get.description:
Browser endpoint (called by Google). Verifies the grant,
enforces the workspace domain, binds the consenting Google
identity to the campus session user (403 on mismatch — nothing
is stored), stores the credential under the integration's
namespaced provider (e.g. `google.classroom`), emits
`campus.integrations.connect` and 302s to the flow's `target`
with its query params preserved. Unlike the identity callback
it never sets the campus login cookie.

Dispatches to the integration proxy's consent handler, which
binds the credential to the campus session user (403 on
mismatch) instead of setting the session, and stores it under
the integration's namespaced provider.

The "who can administer what" matrix query (#872, #883). The operator and the super-admin root (#897,

Authorization: operator for the full matrix; otherwise a

(all optional; unfiltered requires the operator or the

delete.description:
DELETE /logins/<session_id>/

A client-credentials (Basic) caller may revoke any session it owns
without presenting the auth-service session cookie (#692): that
cookie lives in the caller's per-process cookie jar, so a
multi-worker or restarted deployment cannot present the cookie its
own POST /logins established. Session creation is already scoped to
the client's credentials, so client-scoped revocation mirrors the
creation rights.

A Bearer caller may revoke a session record that attributes to its
own user (#837): non-browser clients (the CLI) create their login
session server-side and hold no auth-service cookie, so the
cookie-synced delete path can never work for them. No new risk —
the same bearer can already revoke the underlying token outright
via POST /oauth/revoke. Browser (cookie-carrying) revocation is
unchanged.

get.description: GET /logins/<session_id>/

post.description:
Session-bound token re-acquisition (invariant A10,
docs/auth-token-invariants.md): the session-owning confidential
client exchanges its client secret (Basic) AND the login-session
id for the user's campus bearer — with_user_session()'s lane
after #854 closed the credentials reads it previously relied on.

Issuance mirrors the code exchange: an unexpired grant token is
reused (A3), an expired one is rotated server-side with the
grant record's scopes (A2/A5 — never widened). A missing
credential record is 400 invalid_grant, never minted from
nothing (C5/A5 — revocation forces re-login).

The response omits `refresh_token`: campus refresh material
never leaves the auth service in this lane.

Denials: user bearers 403 (a user principal is never the
session's client, #854), the operator 403 (the credentials
management routes are its path), a non-owning client 403.

POST /logins/<session_id>/token
Authorization: Basic (the session-owning confidential client only).

The session-bound re-acquisition lane (invariant A10,
docs/auth-token-invariants.md): with_user_session() re-acquires the
user's campus bearer after a worker restart or token expiry without
the operator-gated credentials routes (#854) and without re-running
the browser login. The login session plays the authorization code's
role, so the issuance semantics mirror the code exchange
(campus/auth/provider.py::token) with two differences: the grant
record's scopes are the source of truth (A2 — this route never
widens; growth requires a fresh browser flow), and the response
omits the refresh token — campus refresh material never leaves the
auth service in this lane (B2 philosophy); an expired token is
rotated server-side, exactly as the refresh grant does.

A missing credential record is an invalid grant, never minted from
nothing: revoking the campus token (C5) or deleting the record must
force re-login, not resurrect the grant under a live session (A5).

The route serves exactly one principal — the session-owning
confidential client, the #879 session_user_visible ruling extended
from user-record visibility to token issuance. User principals are
denied outright (a user bearer is never the session's client,
#854 — and bearer auth sets current_client to the minting client,
which could otherwise pass the ownership check), and the operator
is denied too: it already holds the credentials management routes,
keeping this route laser-scoped.

Errors: 400 invalid_grant (unknown/expired session, no user on the
session, missing/expired-chain credential), 403 (user principal,
operator, or non-owning client).

get.description:
Clears the auth service's Flask session (the campusauth SSO
session established by identity login) and expires its cookie,
then 302s the browser to the validated target (#785). The
login_sessions record revocation is the API half
(DELETE /auth/v1/logins/{session_id}/). Google's browser
session is deliberately unaffected. Requests with
`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` are signed out but land on "/"
(#797) — first-party apps share the registrable domain and
arrive as `same-site`, keeping their landing.

GET /logout?post_logout_redirect_uri=/some/path

Clears the auth service's Flask session (dropping user_id and the
login session binding) and expires its cookie, then redirects the
browser to the validated target.

Query parameters:
    - post_logout_redirect_uri: same-origin path, or an absolute
      URL whose origin matches a registered client's redirect_uri
      (#788), so sign-out can land the browser back on the calling
      app. The OIDC parameter name is deliberate so #301's optional
      RP-initiated logout (end_session_endpoint) can adopt or
      absorb this endpoint. Absent or unsafe targets fall back to
      "/". Google's browser session is deliberately unaffected:
      signing out of Google itself is a per-app product choice,
      not a framework default (#785, out of scope).

Requests carrying `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` (#797) still get
signed out, but the target is dropped (landing on "/"): first-party
apps share the registrable domain, so the app-initiated hop arrives
as `same-site`, while a foreign page embedding the logout URL gets
the nuisance-grade logout CSRF without the redirect. A missing
header (older browsers) is treated as allowed.

Responses:
    302 Found: Redirect to the validated target.

Browser page (HTML). `GET /device/{user_code}` pre-fills the
code; the page redirects through the Google leg if the user has
no campus login cookie. `POST` is the no-JS form fallback;
`status=success|error` query params drive the fallback states.

This is a web page that users visit to complete the device authorization
flow. They enter the user code displayed by their CLI application.

GET /device - Shows the entry form
GET /device/<user_code> - Pre-fills the user code
GET /device?status=success - Shows success state (for no-JS fallback)
GET /device?status=error&error_code=expired - Shows error state (for no-JS fallback)
POST /device - Handles form submission for non-JS clients

Public. An absent `scope` defaults to the standard CLI scope
set (`read write`); an explicit `scope` (campus-cli --scope
pass-through, #865) is validated fail-closed against the
client's `allowed_scopes` like any other, and the default set
is validated too — either way the request fails with
`invalid_scope` outside the allowlist (invariant A7). The
returned `verification_uri_complete` pre-fills the device
consent page, which discloses the requested scopes before the
user authorizes (#867). Accepts JSON or form-encoded.

POST /oauth/device_authorize
Body: {
    "client_id": "guest",
    "scope": "read write"  # Optional
}
Returns: {
    "device_code": "...",
    "user_code": "ABCD-1234",
    "verification_uri": "https://auth.campus.nyjc.app/device",
    "verification_uri_complete": "https://auth.campus.nyjc.app/device?user_code=ABCD-1234",
    "expires_in": 600,
    "interval": 5
}

An absent or empty scope defaults to the standard CLI scope set
(invariant A1: the default is still validated against the client's
allowlist). Callers such as campus-cli pass --scope through here
(#865); the requested scopes must lie within the client's
registered allowlist or the request is rejected with invalid_scope.

Reference: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8628#section-3.1

Returns 200 regardless of token state (RFC 7009 section 2.2); revoking either token of a pair kills both.
    Accepts JSON or form-encoded.

POST /oauth/revoke
Body: {
    "token": "...",
    "token_type_hint": "access_token" | "refresh_token"  (optional)
    "client_id": "campus-cli"
}
Returns: {} with 200

Per RFC 7009 section 2.2, the response is 200 regardless of
whether the token was found, already revoked, or belongs to
another client — the endpoint does not confirm token validity to
untrusted callers. A missing token is rejected with 400
invalid_request (section 2.1).

client_id carries a None default purely to keep it out of the
required-parameters 422 path: a request without it fails client
validation below with 400 invalid_client, which is also what the
token endpoint does for an unknown client_id.

RFC 6749/8628 token endpoint. The `authorization_code` grant is
NOT handled here — use `POST /auth/v1/token`. The refresh grant
reissues exactly the granted scopes (never widens, invariant
A2) and rotates the token pair; the presented refresh token is
single-use. Accepts JSON or form-encoded bodies. Device-code
polling returns 400 with `authorization_pending`/`slow_down`
until the user approves.

Supports multiple grant types:
- urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code (RFC 8628)
- authorization_code (RFC 6749)
- refresh_token (RFC 6749)
- client_credentials (RFC 6749 section 4.4)

POST /oauth/token
Body (device code): {
    "grant_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code",
    "client_id": "campus-cli",
    "device_code": "..."
}
Body (authorization code): {
    "grant_type": "authorization_code",
    "client_id": "campus-cli",
    "code": "authorization_code",
    "redirect_uri": "https://..."
}
Body (refresh token): {
    "grant_type": "refresh_token",
    "client_id": "campus-cli",
    "refresh_token": "..."
}
Body (client credentials): {
    "grant_type": "client_credentials",
    "client_id": "uid-client-...",
    "client_secret": "..."
}
Returns: {
    "access_token": "...",
    "token_type": "Bearer",
    "expires_in": 3600,
    "refresh_token": "...",  (never present for client_credentials)
    "scope": "read write"
}

post.description:
Server-to-server: the app backend creates the session, then
sends the browser to `GET /authorize` with `state` = the
session id. For `provider=campus`, requested scopes are
validated fail-closed against the client's `allowed_scopes`
(invariant A1/A6); proxy providers carry the upstream
provider's scope strings instead.

For provider="campus", requested scopes are validated fail-closed
against the client's allowed_scopes allowlist (invariant A1/A6,
docs/auth-token-invariants.md).

POST /sessions/{provider}/
Body: {
    "expiry_seconds": 3600,
    "user_id": "user_id",
    "redirect_uri": "https://example.com/callback",
    "scopes": ["scope1", "scope2"],
    "authorization_code": "auth_code",
    "state": "state",
    "target": "https://example.com/target"
}
Returns: {
    "session_token": "new_session_token",
    "expires_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}

post.summary: Look up a session by authorization code

post.description:
Token endpoint for the authorization-code grant (the only grant
handled here). Accepts JSON or form-encoded bodies. The code
binds to the issuing client (RFC 6749 section 4.1.3); the
issued token covers the session's scopes — an existing covering
grant is reused, otherwise a new token carries the union of
grant and request (incremental scope authorization, invariant
A3/A4).

OAuth2 token endpoint for exchanging authorization code for
    access token.

Method:
    POST /token

Path Parameters:
    None

Query Parameters:
    None

Request Body:
    grant_type: str (required)
        Must be "authorization_code".
    code: str (required)
        The authorization code received from `/oauth2/authorize`.
    redirect_uri: str (required)
        Must match the redirect_uri used in authorization.
    client_id: str (required)
        OAuth client identifier.
    client_secret: str (required)
        Secret key for the OAuth client.

Responses:
    400 Invalid authorization code: None
    - Returned when the authorization code in the json does not
      match the one used in the session.
    400 Invalid redirect_uri: None
    - Returned when the redirect_uri does not match the one used in
      the authorization request.
    400 Invalid grant_type: None
    - Returned when grant_type is not "authorization_code"
    401 unauthorized_client: None
    - Returned when the presenting client is not the client the
      authorization code was issued to (RFC 6749 section 4.1.3).
    401 Not authenticated: None
    - Returned when the session ID is not in the Flask session

Scope handling:
    The exchanged token covers every scope of the auth session. If
    the user already holds an unexpired grant for this client that
    covers the requested scopes, that token is reused; otherwise a
    new token is issued with the union of the existing grant and
    the requested scopes (incremental scope authorization,
    docs/auth-token-invariants.md A2-A4).
post.summary: Exchange an authorization code for a Campus token

Internal step of the login chain: called as the Google leg's
target after a successful login. Requires the campus login
cookie; provisions the user record, binds the authorization
code to the session, and 302s the browser to the session's
`redirect_uri` with `code`, `state` and `scope`.

Google auth

Method:
    GET /verify_login

Path Parameters:
    None

Query Parameters:
    state: CampusID - Campus session ID (preserved through Google flow)

Responses:
    302 Found: Redirect to app callback (redirect_uri) with authorization code
    401 Not authenticated: User domain not allowed or no valid Google credential

Read-only view of the in-code integrations registry (#688,
#733): public metadata, the integration's configured scope
cap, and whether the connect flow is open. Computed from the
vault at call time: `connectable` is false for an unconfigured
registry stub or when `CONNECT_TARGETS` is empty — mirroring
the guards the connect route enforces. Public: everything here
is already observable by starting a connect flow; no vault
secrets are ever returned. Consumers build connect links from
`authorize_path`; `scopes` is the cap, not the ask (the
connect flow asks for exactly this set).

GET /integrations/v1/
Auth: public.
Returns: {
    "integrations": [
        {
            "provider": "google.classroom",
            "slug": "classroom",
            "base_provider": "google",
            "title": "Google Classroom",
            "description": "...",
            "scopes": ["..."],      (the integration's scope cap)
            "connectable": true,    (configured AND connect open)
            "authorize_path": "/auth/v1/google/classroom/authorize"
        }
    ]
}

`connectable` is computed from the vault label at call time:
false for an unconfigured registry stub (no upstream OAuth
client) or when CONNECT_TARGETS is empty (connect disabled,
fail-closed) — mirroring the guards the authorize route enforces.
